audit_log.action: ran independent code review (high effort) against branch module-projects-foundation, then fixed all 9 CONFIRMED findings

details.findings_summary: 9 CONFIRMED findings via this project's own code-review skill (8 finder angles, 1-vote verification). Most severe: an IDOR — the five sub-resource repositories (environments, repositories, objectives, team, roadmap items) looked up rows by primary key alone with no projectId in the WHERE clause, letting a user authorized on one project mutate or delete another project's sub-resources by ID. Also found: RoadmapItemsService.update() spread the caller's raw patch (including status) into the repository write, bypassing setActivePhase()'s active-phase invariant and audit logging; setActivePhase()'s three writes were sequential and non-transactional; migration 00043 added a role_permissions.project_id FK the task package's own scope statement never named; an unused (project_id, status) index on roadmap_items and a missing index on projects.updated_at (the real default list-sort column); duplicated toJSON()-plus-date-conversion logic across all six Projects repositories; a speculative single-value provider ENUM column; and dead findById()-style methods on four sub-resource repositories.
details.fixes_applied: Added a shared packages/database/src/projects/entity-mapping.ts helper (closes the duplication finding). Every sub-resource repository's update()/remove() now takes (id, projectId, ...) and scopes its WHERE clause accordingly, threaded through the corresponding dashboard-api services and controllers. RoadmapItemsService.update() now explicitly whitelists only name/sequence. ProjectService.setActivePhase() now wraps all three writes in withTransaction() (the packages/database helper, genuinely unused anywhere in dashboard-api until now). Removed the unused index and added the missing one (migrations 00036/00041). Removed the provider column from migration 00038, entities.ts, and models.ts. Removed the 4 dead findById() methods. Appended a Resolution note to docs/task-packages/module-projects-foundation.md acknowledging the role_permissions.project_id FK as necessary for the IDOR fix, not silent scope creep.

details.findings_summary: 2 CONFIRMED findings via this project's own security-review skill, each independently re-verified at 9/10 confidence by a separate sub-agent pass. High: POST /projects/:projectId/approvers was gated only by project_configuration:approve, which owner_growth_approver itself holds, but minting an RBAC role grant is a users_roles action; the approved matrix (06_Roles_and_Permissions.md section 3) deliberately withholds users_roles:edit from that role (VM, no E) — so any owner_growth_approver could mint unlimited co-approvers on any project they could approve in, a real privilege-escalation path with no other check catching it. Medium: the only role-revocation route, DELETE /authz/users/:userId/roles/:roleId, always called revokeRole() with projectId: null, and UserRoleRepository.revoke() matches the exact (userId, roleId, projectId) triple, so a project-scoped grant could never be revoked through the API — worse, the endpoint always reported revoked: true regardless of whether anything was actually removed.
details.fixes_applied: ProjectApproversService.assign() now performs its own explicit AuthorizationService.evaluate() check for users_roles:edit before delegating to RoleAssignmentService — confirmed against the seeded matrix this makes the endpoint effectively super-admin-only for now, matching the matrix's actual intent rather than inventing a new restriction. RoleAssignmentService.revokeRole() now returns whether a row was actually removed (Promise<boolean>, was Promise<void>), and the controller accepts an optional ?projectId= query param, threading it through so a project-scoped grant can actually be reached, and reports the real outcome instead of always claiming success. Added a new ProjectApproversService unit test proving the users_roles:edit check runs before any role lookup/assignment; two new role-assignment.controller.spec.ts unit tests covering both revoke paths and both outcome values; and two new real-database e2e tests in projects.e2e-spec.ts proving via real HTTP requests that an owner_growth_approver-only session gets a real 403 from the approver endpoint, and that a super_admin-assigned project-scoped grant survives a revoke call missing ?projectId= but is genuinely removed once supplied.
